Commit c7ab5ef9bcd281135c21b4732c9be779585181be entitled ""b43: implement
short slot and basic rate handling"" reduced the transmit throughput for
my BCM4311 device from 18 Mb/s to 0.7 Mb/s. The basic rate handling
portion is OK
column2: the problem is in the short slot handling.

column1: Prior to this change
column2: the short slot enable/disable routines were never

column1: called. Experimentation showed that the critical part was changing the
value at offset 0x0010 in the shared memory. This is supposed to contain
the 802.11 Slot Time in usec
column2: but if it is changed from its initial value

column1: of zero
column2: performance is destroyed. On the other hand

column1: in the MMIO register corresponding to the Interframe Slot Time increased
performance from 18 to 22 Mb/s. A BCM4306/3 also shows dramatic
improvement of the transmit rate from 5.3 to 19.0 Mb/s.
Other changes in the patch include removal of the magic number for the
MMIO register
column2: and allowing the slot time to be set for any PHY operating

column1: in the 2.4 GHz band. Previously
column2: the routine was executed only for G PHYs.
